item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate A is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it exposes the exact required Upload signature, accepts existing FilesOption values, and uses multipartbody.NewFile with the required file field. Candidate B changes the required API and adds explicitly forbidden association machinery.","reasons":["A implements Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption), while B incorrectly introduces UploadFileOption and therefore fails the exact public API contract.","A uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), directly satisfying the established-helper requirement. B expands the helper with NewForm for out-of-scope fields.","A preserves FilesOption query and request-option behavior in Upload. B replaces it with a separate option system and passes no FilesOption query values.","B adds deal, person, organization, product, activity, lead, and project association fields, directly contradicting the instruction not to add association fields or duplicate option machinery. Its changelog and README further advertise the incompatible API."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and error logic instead of routing the encoded body through s.Add as explicitly required.","It makes an unrelated global RawClient retry and ownership change for io.ReadSeeker bodies, contrary to the requested scope; this can change whether caller-provided ReadClosers are closed and introduces shared-seeker replay behavior.","Its tests do not cover propagation of source-reader failures, which the contract specifically requests."],"risks_b":["The Upload signature is contract-incompatible because it accepts UploadFileOption rather than FilesOption.","The new association options and multipart NewForm machinery are explicitly forbidden scope expansion and duplicate existing option patterns.","Upload calls Raw.Do directly rather than routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating request and response behavior while dropping existing FilesOption query semantics entirely. Its tests do not cover source-reader errors either, and it also changes unrelated RawClient retry behavior."]}
